findings.issue: No test catches a target computed from the hands in input order instead of orderHands order. In every fixture (statRecords in AC#3, seeded() in AC#4/AC#5, the unit cases, and the e2e seed) the records array is already in chronological order, so the 'first 1,000 in orderHands order' rule (A-2, SPEC-03) is only checked against a sessionId-order sort, not against skipping the sort. In production trendData() returns IndexedDB key order, which is not chronological, so that bug would ship unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Mutation: I replaced `g2Target(all === data ? order() : orderHands(all))` with `g2Target(all.hands)` in src/stats/trends.ts:219. Then `npx vitest run tests/stats/g2-target.acceptance.test.tsx tests/stats/trends.test.ts` gave 10/10 passing. The file has been restored.
findings.fix: In AC#3, pass the records in non-chronological order, e.g. `dataOf({ ...stored, records: [...records].sort((a, b) => a.sessionId < b.sessionId ? -1 : a.sessionId > b.sessionId ? 1 : a.handNumber - b.handNumber) })` or reversed, and keep the expectedTarget check. In AC#5, also build `all` from a reversed or sessionId-sorted copy so the `orderHands(all)` branch is exercised against shuffled input (the session ids '6','2','c','1' are not in start order, so a sessionId sort changes the first 1,000).

findings.issue: Every pool is seated with the default line-up, so `lineUps` is just ['Custom']. The only line-up filter is therefore the same as 'All', and `sizes` never asserts any line-up count. This meets the spec text ('each lineUp value present in the records'), but it does not show the target staying put under a line-up filter that actually removes hands. AC#5's line-up clause is covered only by the general statisticsView(filtered, all) contract that the game-type and table-size filters already prove. It is not shown directly.
findings.evidence: The builder notes that only 'Custom' is present. seatSession is called without lineUp, so DEFAULT_SESSION_CONFIG.lineUp is 'Custom' (src/table/session.ts:122). The `sizes` toMatchObject has no line-up key.
findings.fix: Seat one pool with a preset line-up. For example, give cashPool/sitAndGoPool an optional config passthrough, or use the existing configForLineUp/lineUpSessionConfig path in session.ts, which is real and not hand-forged. Then assert `lineUps.length >= 2` and add each line-up's expected size to `sizes`. Alternatively, record in the AC#5 test comment that the line-up filter is degenerate until TASK-11.8 and rely on its added AC.

findings.issue: A-3 says that with a non-null g2Target, a 'more-hands' or 'no-hands' Major chart shows no caption and no line. Nothing asserts this. The code is correct today (the caption and line render only inside MajorErrorTrend, under chart?.kind === 'points'), but if the caption were moved outside, no test would fail.
findings.evidence: No test renders a view with g2Target non-null and chart.kind !== 'points'. The closest case, statisticsView(few, data), uses 500 hands and so plots points.
findings.fix: Add to the SPEC-06 unit or AC#4: `statisticsView(firstFourHundredRecords, all)`. Expect g2Target to be 3.1, the rendered Major card to contain `stats-message`, and it to contain neither `stats-target` nor G2_CAPTION.

summary: The implementation matches the spec. g2Target sums unhintedMajors over the first 1,000 hands of the orderHands-ordered `all` (every game type, size and line-up) and rounds with bbPer100(m, 2, 1000). statisticsView(data, all = data) always takes the target from `all` and reuses the ordering only when all === data. The caption and the dashed line render only inside the points branch. yMax includes the target. With a null target the markup is byte-identical, which the unit test pins with the exact pre-change string. Scope, CSS and fixture changes match §5, gates pass, and the stats tests pass locally. AC#3 and AC#5 recompute the target independently (expectedTarget sorts by startedAt and hand number). AC#5 derives each view's y from its own yMax, and computing from `data` instead of `all` fails in the Cash, Sit-and-go and Full ring views. Main gap (MAJOR): every fixture already lists hands chronologically, so skipping the sort in the target path survives all tests (shown by mutation). On the builder's line-up remark: the AC#5 line-up filter sees only 'Custom', so it is the same as 'All' and does not prove the line-up clause directly. AC#5 holds only through the filter-agnostic (filtered, all) contract (MINOR).
